correctness.rationale: Partial injective idempotents are partial identities. A strict-arrow graph is a directed path forest with n-r components, giving exactly 2^(n-r) commuting partial identities. Strict maps correspond by image shift to a smaller i-Catalan monoid, counted by Narayana reflection. Splitting at fixed points proves F=S/(1-zS) and all k tuple counts. Algebraic discriminant/pole analysis, including u=(3-sqrt5)/2, proves the stated asymptotic constants in all three regimes. The standalone verification uses independent composition enumeration for all specified finite cases; computations do not substitute for the general proof.

originality.rationale: Full-source comparison finds known i-Catalan cardinalities, known k=1 numerical OGF/asymptotics (OEIS A225887), and classical weighted lattice-path machinery. The independent claimed result is instead a full relative-idempotent-centralizer spectrum and every k>=2 simultaneous moment with pole transition; the cited prior single specialization does not imply those claims. Publication priority is best-knowledge and a more general unseen weighted enumeration is a residual risk.

value.rationale: The Boolean idempotent semilattice is canonical and common commutants of multiple idempotents are natural monoid invariants. A complete distribution for all chain sizes, exact multivariate simultaneous tuple moments, and a sharp transition between square-root and pole behavior for k=1 versus k>=2 give a motivated structural and asymptotic classification, beyond the known one-parameter numerical sequence.
